page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 virtual instance powered by 16 physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs from the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor family operating at 2.5 GHz. Allocated on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU resources, it includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage and features no dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported at a baseline rate of 10 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon architecture features 35 MB of L3 cache alongside 1 MB L2 cache per core and 32 KB L1 data cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI, enabling hardware acceleration for vector operations and neural network inference routines. Cryptographic and bit manipulation instruction sets like AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA are supported natively. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate cached read performance of 1557.61 GB/sec and uncached read and write throughput of 109.69 GB/sec and 47.96 GB/sec respectively.

Benchmark evaluations reveal average multi-core and general compute performance, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 27240.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10181.0. Single-core throughput is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 25 percent and single-threaded gzip compression yielding 22.88 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations scale efficiently, achieving 127.99 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 26.78 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. The instance offers resource density for compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks, software compilation with Clang, static web serving, and distributed back-end microservices requiring sustained multi-vCPU compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores based on the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, combined with 64.0 GB of RAM. Running on a KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, this instance features AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction support, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight average multi-core throughput, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 27240.11, a Geekbench multi-core score of 10181.0, and a Redis SET capability of 26.78 million operations per second. Single-core performance remains limited, as shown by lower stress-ng single-core metrics. Given its 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio, the instance provides cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density suitable for parallel batch processing, software compilation, static web serving, and microservice workloads.
